title: Two Unvaccinated Pennsylvanians Die of Measles in First US Deaths This Year
excerpt: Lancaster County deaths mark Pennsylvania's first measles fatalities in 35 years as the US endures its worst outbreak since 1991 with nearly 2,800 cases.
body:
• Two unvaccinated residents of Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, have died from measles — the first measles deaths in the US in 2026 and the first in Pennsylvania in 35 years
  • Pennsylvania has confirmed 393 measles cases this year, with 185 concentrated in Lancaster County; nationwide cases have reached 2,777, the worst year since 1991
  • Governor Josh Shapiro declined federal assistance from HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., telling him that vaccine misinformation "has real-life consequences"
  • The MMR vaccine provides 97% lifetime protection when administered in two doses, yet US kindergarten vaccination rates have slipped below the 95% threshold needed to prevent outbreaks

Two unvaccinated Pennsylvania residents have died from measles, the state Department of Health announced Tuesday, marking the first measles-related deaths in the United States this year and the first in the Commonwealth in 35 years.

Both individuals lived in Lancaster County, the epicenter of Pennsylvania's outbreak, which has recorded 185 of the state's 393 confirmed cases in 2026. State health officials declined to reveal additional details about the deceased to protect their families' privacy.

The Worst Year in Three Decades

The deaths come as the US endures its worst measles year since 1991. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed 2,777 cases as of August 20, already surpassing 2025's record-breaking total of 2,289. At least 36 new outbreaks have been recorded across 46 states this year.

https://x.com/MeidasTouch/status/2092339258518610313

The numbers reflect a measles resurgence driven by declining vaccination coverage. CDC data shows 94% of new cases involved people who were unvaccinated or whose vaccination status was unknown. None of the cases in Pennsylvania involved fully vaccinated individuals.

"Because measles was largely eliminated in the Commonwealth for more than three decades, people are not familiar with this disease and don't fully understand the potential severity of the illness."

— Dr. Debra Bogen, Pennsylvania Secretary of Health

Shapiro Rebukes Kennedy on Vaccine Misinformation

The political dimension of the outbreak sharpened on Tuesday when HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. called Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro to offer federal staff for the measles response. Shapiro said he declined the offer, telling Kennedy that the state could manage with its own resources — and that vaccine misinformation was having real consequences.

"There's real-life consequences to spreading misinformation. There's real-life consequences to scaring people and not relying on actual doctors and actual medical professionals to provide unbiased information to parents so that we can make reasonable decisions for our kids."

— Josh Shapiro, Pennsylvania Governor

Kennedy visited Lancaster County in 2021 while leading the anti-vaccine organization Children's Health Defense, where he made light of his own childhood measles case and stoked fears about vaccines. During his time as HHS Secretary, vaccination rates have continued to fall nationwide.

Vaccination Rates Below Critical Threshold

The outbreak underscores a widening gap in vaccine coverage. US kindergarten MMR vaccination rates slipped to 92.5% in the 2024-2025 school year — below the 95% threshold public health officials say is necessary to prevent outbreaks through herd immunity. The share of kindergartners with vaccine exemptions rose to an all-time high of 3.6%.

Lancaster County, known as the heart of Pennsylvania's Amish community, had only 88% of kindergartners up to date on measles vaccines during the last school year. Measles is exceptionally contagious — one infected person can transmit the virus to 12 to 18 others in an unvaccinated population.

Nearly 20% of people who contract measles require hospitalization. While deaths are relatively rare, occurring in one to three cases per 1,000, the disease can cause severe complications including pneumonia and brain swelling. In November, international health officials will meet to determine if the US has lost its measles-free status, which it achieved in 2000.

Back-to-School Urgency

With the school year beginning across the country, health officials are urging parents to verify their children's vaccination status. The MMR vaccine, administered in two doses typically between ages one and five, provides 97% lifetime protection against measles. Adults and teenagers who are unsure of their vaccination history should also consult their healthcare providers.
